newsitem.title: INDIA: Six killed in Kashmir gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Six killed in Kashmir gunbattle.

text.p: Four separatist guerrillas and two Indian soldiers were killed during a fierce 20-hour gunbattle in Kashmir, an Indian defence spokesman said on Friday.
"Four foreign militants were killed in an encounter with the army near Pandach which erupted when an army patrol was attacked last evening by militants," Major P. Purshuttam said.
Pandach is a residential area in northern Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, mostly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state.
"Two army soldiers were also killed in the operation, which ended this afternoon," he said.
At least 10 houses were gutted by fires triggered by the gunbattle, the spokesman said. A large quantity of arms and ammunition was recovered.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting for either independence from Indian rule or merger with neighbouring Pakistan.

India, which controls two thirds of Kashmir, accuses Pakistan of arming and training the separatist guerrillas. Pakistan, which rules the remaining one third, says it only provides political and diplomatic support to Kashmiri separatists.

Police and hospitals say about 20,000 people have been killed in insurgency-related violence since the separatist revolt erupted in 1990, but separatist leaders and the state chief minister Farooq Abdullah say some 50,000 have died.
